oral_epics.ability_reason: Trained reciters keep long accounts; the people's memory outlives any single teller.

named_landmark_lore.name: Every Notable Rock and Spring Has a Naming Story

bone_flutes_drums.observation: A bone flute and a skin drum carry the song at gatherings, and the young learn the tunes of their elders.

circle_dances.observation: The whole camp joins a circle dance, and a quarrel is hard to keep up with a neighbor whose hand you hold.

house_floor_burial.observation: The dead are buried beneath the house floor, so the family lives on above its own ancestors.
house_floor_burial.social_consequence: The dead stay close to the living, and so does their sickness

ochre_grave_goods.observation: The dead are laid in red ochre with beads and tools for the journey after life.

kin_body_ornament.observation: Paint, shells and beads mark which kin a person belongs to, so strangers are known at a glance.

hearth_shrine_offerings.observation: Each household sets aside a share of its meal at the hearth-shrine for the living god.

plastered_ancestor_skulls.observation: The skulls of honored ancestors are plastered with faces and kept in the house, where their names are spoken.

mourning_days.observation: For set days after a death the household wails and fasts, and neighbors leave them to grieve.

festival_calendar.ability_reason: Shared festivals gather scattered households at set seasons, binding them and timing their work together.

reciprocal_gift_exchange.observation: A gift must be returned in time, and the chain of gifts binds households that would otherwise be strangers.

origin_story.observation: Reciters tell how the people and their god came to this land, and every child can tell it back.

pottery_style_identity.observation: Potters paint the motifs of their own people, and a sherd tells where it was made.

ancestor_figurines.observation: Small clay figures of ancestors stand in the house and receive a share of food on feast days.

pit_pebble_game.observation: Children and elders sow pebbles around rows of pits and learn to count ahead to win.

first_fruits_offering.observation: No one eats the new harvest until its first fruits have been given to the god.

winter_tale_nights.observation: On long winter nights the old tales are told by the fire, and the young correct a teller who strays.

named_star_figures.observation: The stars are grouped into figures from the stories, and a traveler finds his way by the hunter and the plow.

shrine_wall_painting.observation: The walls of the shrine room are painted with the god's beasts and the people's hunts.

ritual_masks_costumes.observation: In mask and costume the dancers become the god's creatures for the length of the rite.

sacred_places.observation: A spring, a grove and a high rock are set apart for the god; no one cuts, hunts or builds there.

coming_of_age_rites.observation: Youths are taught the people's secrets and duties at a set rite, and return as adults.

cross_craft_visiting.name: Crafters Spend a Season Watching Another Craft

memorial_cairn_marking.name: Memorial Cairns at the Sites of Notable Events

marriage_feasts.observation: A marriage is sealed with a feast where two lineages eat together and exchange gifts.

first_shrine_house.observation: The people raise a house for the god, larger than any dwelling, where offerings and gatherings now take place.
first_shrine_house.ability_reason: The god has a house: rites, offerings and gatherings gain a fixed center, and the people's devotion a visible form.
first_shrine_house.social_consequence: The shrine's keepers become a new voice in the settlement, speaking for the god

praise_songs.observation: Songs of praise are sung to the god at set hours, and every voice knows the words.

rattles_drums_pipes.observation: Clay rattles, fired drums and reed pipes give work songs and festivals a fuller sound.

traveling_storyteller_exchange.name: Traveling Storytellers Trade Tales for Lodging

graveside_libations.observation: Families pour water and beer at the graves so the ancestors do not thirst.

festival_wrestling_races.observation: At festivals the young men wrestle and race, and the winners are praised in song.

emblem_processions.observation: The god's emblem is carried around the fields in procession to bless the crops.

proverbs.observation: Short sayings carry hard-won counsel: plant after the second rain; do not trust a dry well.

temple_festival_meals.observation: At the great festivals the god's house feeds the whole town from its stores.

flood_origin_stories.observation: Stories tell of the great flood and the first days, and of the ones who built high and survived.

rank_inlay_ornament.observation: Shell and stone inlay mark the high-ranking, and only they may wear it.
rank_inlay_ornament.social_consequence: Authority hardens into rank; order and reach improve, but households outside the ruling line lose their voice

seasonal_commemoration_rites.name: A Yearly Rite on the Date of a Remembered Disaster

public_debate_custom.name: Rival Explanations Argued Before the Community

rank_dress_styles.observation: Hair and dress mark age and rank, and a man who dresses above his station is shamed.

craft_lineage_naming.name: Techniques Credited to the Teacher Who Began Them

visiting_specialist_consultations.name: Respected Outsiders Consulted on Hard Disputes

stone_relief_carving.observation: Carvers cut scenes of offering and victory into stone slabs that will outlast every painted wall.

banded_procession_vessels.observation: Tall vessels show the offering procession in bands, from the gift-bearers to the god himself.

temple_singers_lamenters.observation: Singers and lamenters trained in the god's house keep its hymns and dirges exactly.

guest_friendship.observation: Houses in different towns bind themselves as guest-friends, sheltering and helping each other's travelers.

founder_story_recitation.observation: At the turn of the year the founder's story is recited before the whole town.

board_race_games.observation: Players race pieces around a marked board by the throw of sticks, and wager on the outcome.

new_year_festival.observation: Each new year the god renews the land: the whole town gathers for days of rites, processions and feasting.
new_year_festival.ability_reason: The whole town renews itself with the god each year; loyalties are restated and the year's work begins together.
new_year_festival.social_consequence: The festival binds the town to its god and to the steward who presides over it

town_identity.observation: The town has its own name, emblem and patron festival, and its people call themselves by it.

theophoric_names.observation: Parents name children for the god: the god-is-gracious, the god-has-given.

votive_figures.observation: Worshippers set carved figures of themselves before the god to pray without ceasing on their behalf.

seasonal_hymn_cycles.observation: Each season of the god's year has its own cycle of hymns, sung in order from first to last.

harps_and_lyres.observation: Tuned harps and lyres, their frames joined and strung, accompany hymns and feasts.

chamber_tombs.observation: Leading lineages build stone chambers for their dead, filled with rich goods and sometimes servants.
chamber_tombs.social_consequence: Great tombs proclaim the ruling line's permanence, and the labor to build them comes from everyone else

temple_choirs.observation: Choirs with drums and cymbals fill the god's courtyard on feast days.

comparative_craft_gatherings.name: Craft Specialists Compare Methods on Market Days

inlaid_mosaic_panels.observation: Panels of shell, stone and bitumen show feasts and processions in rows of tiny inlaid figures.

wisdom_instructions.observation: A father's instructions to his son are copied and taught: speak little, pay debts, respect the god.

festival_dancers_acrobats.observation: Dancers and acrobats perform at festivals before crowds from the whole district.

officiant_vestments.observation: Officiants wear garments and headdresses no one else may wear, and the rite is not valid without them.

envoy_reception.observation: Foreign envoys are received with a feast and gifts, and send gifts back by the same road.

calendar_feast_days.observation: Feast days are fixed to the months of the god's calendar, and work stops for them across the land.

royal_mourning.observation: When the ruler dies, the whole land laments for set days before the heir is acclaimed.

royal_stone_portraits.observation: Portraits of the ruler in stone stand in the temples, praying for him when he is absent.

royal_wrestling_matches.observation: Wrestlers and boxers fight before the ruler, who rewards the champions.

dream_interpretation.observation: Dreams are told to the god's servants, who read them as messages and warnings.

debate_poems.observation: Poems set two rivals arguing in verse, the hoe against the plow, summer against winter, and the audience judges.

heroic_song_cycle.observation: Songs of a great ruler's deeds are sung and written down as a cycle every child and soldier knows.
heroic_song_cycle.ability_reason: The people share a written epic of their own greatness; memory, loyalty and courage are passed on together.
heroic_song_cycle.social_consequence: The hero's glory lends luster to his heirs, whatever their own deeds

royal_ancestor_offerings.observation: Each month offerings are laid for the dead rulers, whose names are read out in order.

love_wedding_songs.observation: Love songs and wedding songs are sung at every marriage, and the young learn them by heart.

city_laments.observation: Laments mourn a ruined town street by street, so its fall is never forgotten.

offering_omens.observation: Diviners read the god's will in the entrails of offerings before any great decision.

god_boat_procession.observation: The god's image rides in a sacred boat carried through the streets and along the river.

letters_to_the_god.observation: Petitioners write letters to the god and lay them before the shrine.

palace_wall_painting.observation: The palace halls are painted with tribute, processions and the ruler's victories.

scribal_songs_satires.observation: Tablet-house students trade songs and satires about lazy pupils and cruel teachers.

pilgrimage.observation: Pilgrims come from distant towns to the god's great house for the new year, bringing gifts and news.
pilgrimage.social_consequence: Pilgrim roads spread news, trade and sickness alike

foreign_fashion_adoption.observation: Foreign ornament and dress become fashionable among the wealthy, and the old styles look provincial.
foreign_fashion_adoption.social_consequence: Openness to foreign ways brings new goods and ideas, and some who resent them

sung_divine_narrative.observation: The god's deeds are sung as a long narrative with music at the great festivals.

feast_of_the_dead.observation: Once a year every household feasts with its dead, setting places for them at the table.

festival_bread_sharing.observation: Bread baked from the god's grain is shared with every household at the festival.
